session_mechanics: Use one challenge per sitting unless the learner explicitly requests a combined path.
Hints are opt-in and level-gated; do not volunteer them.
Evaluation only runs when the learner says 'evaluate'.
follow_up_complications are stretch work and should be scored separately if used.

time_budget_guidance.main: One difficulty-4 challenge (30-40 min) or a full case (75-90 min).
time_budget_guidance.stretch: One follow_up_complication per session, not more.
time_budget_guidance.review: One review_exercise per weak topic identified during evaluation.

score_combination: Per-challenge rubric scores are independent; do not average across families.
Track weak topics by frequency of occurrence across sessions, not by single-session score.
Use mistake_categories to weight review priorities: DESIGN and TRADEOFF mistakes compound across challenges; SQL mistakes are local.

glossary.grain: The exact meaning of one row in a fact table.
glossary.additive: A measure that can be summed across every dimension.
glossary.semi_additive: A measure that can be summed across some dimensions but not others (typically not time).
glossary.non_additive: A measure that cannot be summed across any dimension (ratios, percentages).
glossary.conformed_dimension: A dimension shared across multiple fact tables with consistent meaning and keys.
glossary.degenerate_dimension: A dimension key stored directly on the fact without its own dimension table.
glossary.accumulating_snapshot: A fact whose row is updated as a process moves through milestones.
glossary.periodic_snapshot: A fact capturing state at regular intervals.
glossary.transactional_fact: A fact capturing an event at the moment it occurs.
glossary.factless_fact: A fact table with no measures, capturing relationships or events.
glossary.scd_type_2: History preserved by adding a new row for each change with validity dates.
glossary.scd_type_3: History preserved by adding a previous-value column.
glossary.scd_type_6: Hybrid of types 1, 2 and 3 in one dimension.
glossary.bridge_table: A table resolving a many-to-many relationship between a fact and a dimension.
glossary.fanout: Row multiplication caused by joining tables at different grains.
glossary.watermark: A threshold for deciding when late data is no longer expected.
glossary.idempotent: A write operation that produces the same result when repeated.
glossary.event_time: When the event occurred in the source world.
glossary.processing_time: When the event was processed by the pipeline.
glossary.point_in_time_correctness: Using only the data that was known at the moment being modeled.
glossary.cdc: Change Data Capture: extracting inserts, updates and deletes from a source.
glossary.medallion: A layered lakehouse pattern: bronze (raw), silver (validated), gold (curated).
glossary.inferred_member: A dimension row created for a business key that has not yet arrived in the source.
glossary.gap_and_island: A technique using date-minus-row-number to detect consecutive runs.
glossary.conceptual_model: A business-level model of entities and relationships, independent of any database.
glossary.logical_model: A technology-neutral representation as tables, columns and keys.
glossary.physical_model: A database-specific representation with types, constraints, indexes and storage.
glossary.logical_type: A type description independent of any DBMS (identifier, text, monetary, date).
glossary.artifact: A concrete deliverable the learner must produce (diagram, DDL, query, matrix).

mistake_category_examples.KNOWLEDGE: Confusing Type 2 with Type 1 SCD; misstating a normal form; not knowing TRY_CAST exists.
mistake_category_examples.APPLICATION: Correctly naming a concept but applying it to the wrong grain or wrong level (conceptual vs logical).
mistake_category_examples.REQUIREMENTS: Missing or misreading a stated constraint (e.g., ignoring 'exclusive ValidTo').
mistake_category_examples.DESIGN: Fanout join, one fact for two processes, or dimension without history.
mistake_category_examples.SQL: Wrong join keys, missing tie handling, incorrect window frame, unsafe CAST.
mistake_category_examples.TRADEOFF: Choosing a technology or methodology without stating costs or alternatives.
mistake_category_examples.COMMUNICATION: Correct answer not explainable to a stakeholder; unclear grain statement; unreadable diagram.

anti_patterns_catalog: One universal fact table for every process.
Natural IDs used as warehouse keys without source-system namespace.
Summing semi-additive measures across time.
Joining many-to-many tables directly to a fact and duplicating measures.
Overwriting historical dimension attributes in place.
Deleting reversed or cancelled transactions instead of preserving them.
Using the current dimension row for historical facts.
One diagnosis / phone / category column per entity.
Choosing a methodology or platform without stating tradeoffs.
Retrying an entire pipeline instead of resuming from a checkpoint.
Exactly-once claims without an idempotency mechanism.
No raw replay layer for stream processing.
Recomputing published reports with new classifications.
Fraud or ML features built with data unavailable at prediction time.
Storing PII in every fact row.
Recursive CTE without a cycle guard.
Window frame with default RANGE on non-unique ordering.
Putting foreign keys in a conceptual model.
Using SQL types in a logical model.
Casting free-text columns with unsafe CAST instead of TRY_CAST.
COALESCE to zero to hide NULL semantics.
Silently dropping rows during cleaning.
Non-idempotent in-place UPDATE cleaning.

evaluation_examples.weak_answer: Joins FactSales to DimProduct and DimStore, groups by region and product, orders by revenue desc, returns top 3 with ROW_NUMBER.
why_weak: ROW_NUMBER drops ties; requirement says include ties.
Date filter uses GETDATE() without deriving the last completed quarter.
Ranking on raw rows, not aggregated region-product revenue.
evaluation_examples.strong_answer_sketch: CTE aggregates revenue by region and product within the completed quarter, filters SaleStatus, then DENSE_RANK partitioned by region, and returns rows where rank <= 3.

review_plan.principle: One focused review exercise per weak topic, chosen from the bank's review_exercise fields.
procedure: After evaluation, list the top two weak topics.
For each, pick the review_exercise from the challenge where the weak topic appeared.
If the same weak topic appears in more than one challenge, prefer the lowest-difficulty review_exercise.
Reassess after two sessions; if the weak topic persists, move the learner back one step in prerequisite_graph.

prompt_templates.student: Act as my Data Engineering practice instructor. Do not solve the challenge or reveal its hidden topics. Let me work through every task. Clarify requirements when necessary, but do not suggest a technology, schema, key, fact type, dimension type or architecture unless I explicitly request a hint. If I provide a partial answer, ask questions that expose gaps without completing it. Wait until I request evaluation.
prompt_templates.hint: Give only the requested hint level. Level 1 points toward the decision, Level 2 names the relevant concept, and Level 3 gives a strong directional hint without presenting the complete solution.
prompt_templates.evaluation: Evaluate technical correctness, internal consistency, requirements coverage and reasoning. Accept multiple defensible solutions. Score each rubric category, explain strengths and improvements, identify important mistakes, assign mistake categories, list weak topics, and propose one focused review exercise.

challenges.title: Food Aid Inventory Across Country Offices

student.scenario: An international NGO receives donated goods in five countries. Each country records shipments, warehouse receipts, delivery orders and beneficiaries in a separate operational database. Headquarters needs consolidated inventory and distribution reporting without slowing local operations.
requirements: Daily quantity received, on hand and distributed by country, warehouse, product and donor
Historical reporting when beneficiary classifications or product categories change
A single shipment may contain several lots and expiration dates
Country systems use overlapping product and beneficiary IDs
tasks: Separate operational and analytical responsibilities
Define the required fact tables and the grain of each
Identify conformed dimensions and key strategy
Explain how balances should aggregate across warehouses and dates
Sketch the daily pipeline and two data-quality checks
constraints: Daily refresh by 06:00 UTC
Seven years of history
Local systems must remain available during extraction

internal.assessment_focus: The learner should distinguish distribution events from inventory balances and prevent summing balances across time.
common_traps: One fact table for every process
Summing quantity on hand across dates

hints: Ask whether a delivery and a midnight balance describe the same kind of event.
Consider separate transactional and periodic-snapshot facts.
Quantity on hand is additive across products and warehouses, but not across snapshot dates.
follow_up_complications: One country begins sending stock changes every five minutes.
Headquarters requires the beneficiary category as it existed on the delivery date.
A shipment correction arrives two weeks after month-end close.
challenges.review_exercise: Given a small sample of shipment and snapshot rows, write two grain statements and one aggregation query that must not sum across snapshot dates.

challenges.title: Bank Balances and Customer Transactions

student.scenario: A regional bank stores every account transaction and a balance for each account at midnight. Analysts need transaction volume, average daily balance and end-of-month balance by branch and customer segment.
requirements: Preserve customer segment history
Accounts may move to another branch
Reversed transactions must remain auditable
Reports must support daily and monthly analysis
tasks: Define the business processes
Choose fact-table types and grains
Classify the principal measures by additivity
Design dimensions and history handling
Explain how to calculate end-of-month and average balances without double counting
constraints: Ten years of history
Balances can be corrected after arrival

internal.assessment_focus: Balances and flows require different facts and aggregation behavior.
common_traps: Summing daily balances across a month

hints: Separate movements from states.
Transaction amount and account balance do not aggregate identically across time.
Use a transaction fact for movements and a daily snapshot for balances; select the last valid date for month-end.
follow_up_complications: Finance asks for intraday balances every 15 minutes.
A customer can jointly own several accounts.
Branch reorganizations must be reported both historically and under the current hierarchy.
challenges.review_exercise: Classify five measures as additive, semi-additive or non-additive and state the correct aggregation path for each.

challenges.title: Hospital Encounters, Beds and Outcomes

student.scenario: A hospital network wants analytics for patient encounters, bed occupancy, diagnoses, procedures and discharge outcomes. Operational systems differ by hospital and update throughout the day.
requirements: Daily occupancy by ward
Length of stay and time between admission milestones
Multiple diagnoses and procedures per encounter
Patient privacy and restricted analyst access
tasks: Identify business processes and grains
Choose fact-table types
Model many-valued diagnoses and procedures
Design date/time roles
Propose a privacy-aware analytical access strategy
constraints: Dashboards refresh hourly
Personally identifiable data must be minimized
Late discharge updates are common

internal.assessment_focus: The model should support milestones, occupancy states and multivalued clinical classifications.
common_traps: Using only the current discharge status

hints: Admission has milestones; occupancy is a recurring state.
An accumulating snapshot can track lifecycle dates, while a periodic snapshot supports occupancy.
Many diagnoses per encounter may require a bridge or factless association table.
follow_up_complications: Patients may be transferred between wards several times.
Regulators request deletion or de-identification of selected patient data.
A new hospital uses different diagnosis codes.
challenges.review_exercise: Model one encounter with two diagnoses and one procedure at both a bridge-table grain and a periodic-snapshot grain, then explain why both are needed.

challenges.title: University Enrollment and Student Progress

student.scenario: A university wants reporting on applications, enrollment, course registrations, grades and graduation. Students can change majors, take a course more than once and enroll in more than one program.
requirements: Enrollment counts by term and program
Retention cohorts
Grade distribution by course and instructor
Historical major at the time of registration
tasks: Define facts and grains
Resolve student-program and course-attempt cardinalities
Choose dimension history strategies
Identify role-playing date dimensions
Describe one cohort-retention SQL approach
constraints: Semester and short-course calendars coexist
Legacy student IDs can be reused after migration

internal.assessment_focus: Each course attempt must be preserved and program membership must be modeled over time.
common_traps: Course code as globally unique key

hints: A student can generate several distinct events in the same course.
State the grain with student, course offering, term and attempt.
Treat changing majors historically and isolate reused source IDs with a durable warehouse key.
follow_up_complications: The university acquires another institution with overlapping IDs.
Management wants near-real-time registration dashboards.
A course may be co-taught by several instructors.
challenges.review_exercise: Write a single grain statement that survives a student taking the same course twice under two different majors.

challenges.title: Telecom Usage and Billing Reconciliation

student.scenario: A telecom receives billions of call-detail and data-usage records each day. Operations needs dashboards within two minutes; finance needs an exact daily billable total reconciled to the billing system.
requirements: Near-real-time network usage
Daily authoritative revenue reconciliation
Duplicate and out-of-order events
Customer plans and cell-tower attributes change over time
tasks: Design a combined streaming and batch architecture
Define event identity and deduplication
Select analytical grains
Explain history handling
Define freshness and reconciliation metrics
constraints: Three billion events per day
Events can arrive 24 hours late
Dashboard availability is more important than perfect immediate completeness

internal.assessment_focus: The design must explicitly separate provisional low-latency results from authoritative reconciled results.
common_traps: One SLA for operations and finance

hints: The two consumers do not require the same balance of latency and correctness.
Think about a fast provisional path plus an authoritative replayable path.
Use stable event IDs, idempotent writes, watermarks and daily batch reconciliation.
follow_up_complications: A region goes offline for six hours and later uploads all events.
Finance disputes a completed month after a tariff correction.
Retention rules require raw event deletion after 90 days.
challenges.review_exercise: Write two SLAs (freshness and completeness) for the same dataset and explain why a single number cannot satisfy both consumers.

challenges.title: E-Commerce Returns and Profitability

student.scenario: An online retailer reports revenue correctly but cannot explain profitability after partial returns, discounts, taxes, shipping and exchange-rate changes.
requirements: Line-level revenue and cost
Partial returns months after purchase
Reports in local and corporate currency
Promotion and product-category history
tasks: Define transaction grains for sales and returns
Choose how to link returns to original sales
Classify measures by additivity
Design currency-rate handling
Propose a net-profit query approach
constraints: Orders may contain multiple currencies only through later settlement adjustments
Exchange rates are supplied daily

internal.assessment_focus: The model must preserve gross events and support net calculations without overwriting history.

hints: Do not erase the original economic event.
Returns can be separate transactions linked to the original line.
Store monetary components at a consistent line-event grain and make the applied exchange-rate date explicit.
follow_up_complications: Shipping cost exists only at order level.
A return is refunded at a different exchange rate.
Finance changes its definition of contribution margin.
challenges.review_exercise: Write one sentence per measure stating its grain and additivity.

challenges.title: City Transit Reliability

student.scenario: A city collects GPS pings from buses, scheduled timetables, ticket validations and maintenance records. It wants route reliability, passenger demand and vehicle downtime analysis.
requirements: Vehicle positions every 10 seconds
Daily on-time performance
Ridership by route and stop
Historical route and stop changes
tasks: Place each source in an appropriate ingestion and storage path
Define analytical business processes and grains
Explain batch versus streaming use
Handle route-version history
Propose performance storage formats
constraints: GPS produces semi-structured events
Five-year analytical retention
Operations dashboard target latency is 30 seconds

internal.assessment_focus: The learner should avoid forcing every raw GPS event directly into a reporting star without a suitable raw/processing layer.
common_traps: Treating route name as stable key

hints: Raw telemetry and curated reporting tables have different schema needs.
Use flexible raw storage before validated, schema-on-write analytical models.
Version route/stop definitions and aggregate or derive trip-level reliability facts for reporting.
follow_up_complications: GPS data contains long gaps in tunnels.
The city changes the definition of on-time performance.
A new payment provider sends duplicated validations.
challenges.review_exercise: Place four sources (GPS, timetable, ticket, maintenance) into raw, processing and serving layers with one justification each.

challenges.title: Manufacturing Quality and Sensor Data

student.scenario: A manufacturer combines production orders, machine sensor readings, inspections and defects. Engineers want real-time anomaly detection; management wants monthly yield and cost reporting.
requirements: Sensor readings at millisecond frequency
Trace each finished unit to production batch and machine
Defects may be reclassified later
Monthly yield must remain reproducible
tasks: Design storage and processing layers
Define facts at sensor, inspection and production grains
Choose history strategy for defect classifications
Separate real-time and governed reporting outputs
Specify lineage and quality controls
constraints: Petabyte-scale sensor history
Only 13 months of raw high-frequency data are retained
Regulatory reports must reproduce prior published totals

internal.assessment_focus: Different resolutions and consumers require tiered data and reproducible curated outputs.
common_traps: Keeping every sensor point forever in the warehouse
Recomputing old reports with new classifications

hints: Ask which data needs millisecond detail and for how long.
Separate raw telemetry, derived features and governed reporting facts.
Freeze or version the semantic inputs used for published regulatory periods.
follow_up_complications: A defective sensor produced biased values for three weeks.
Management wants cross-factory benchmarking despite different machine models.
A regulator requests the exact data lineage for one batch.
challenges.review_exercise: Draw a three-tier retention policy (raw, downsampled, governed) and state what each tier must preserve.

challenges.title: BlueCart International Commerce Platform

student.scenario: BlueCart operates e-commerce businesses in eight countries. PostgreSQL stores orders, MySQL stores inventory, a CRM stores customers, suppliers send CSV files, a REST API provides exchange rates and JSON captures web events.
requirements: Revenue and margin
Historical inventory
Customer segmentation
Fulfillment performance
Historical geography and product category
Near-real-time web funnels
Daily finance reconciliation
tasks: Classify source workloads and data types
Choose warehouse/lake/lakehouse components and justify them
Design ingestion, staging and transformation flows
Apply Kimball's four steps to each business process
Define fact grains and dimensions
Choose SCD and key strategies
Write SQL logic for quarterly top-three products per region
Define security, quality, observability and recovery
constraints: Five billion web events per month
Finance closes by 08:00 local time
Product and customer IDs overlap after acquisitions

internal.assessment_focus: A coherent end-to-end design matters more than naming a fashionable platform.

hints: List business processes before listing tables.
Sales, inventory, fulfillment and web behavior have different grains and latency requirements.
Use conformed dimensions across stars, durable source-key mapping, and a separate low-latency web path with governed reconciliation.
follow_up_complications: BlueCart acquires a competitor with overlapping IDs and different currencies.
GDPR deletion requests must be fulfilled without corrupting aggregate finance history.
The nightly transformation exceeds its six-hour window.
challenges.review_exercise: Produce a one-page bus matrix (business processes vs conformed dimensions) for BlueCart.

challenges.title: Global Health Supply Chain

student.scenario: A global health organization purchases medicines, receives donations, ships containers, manages country warehouses and distributes goods to clinics. Data arrives from ERP tables, Access databases, spreadsheets and scanned shipment documents.
requirements: End-to-end shipment status
Stock by lot and expiration date
Distribution to clinics and programs
Wastage and ineffective-use analysis
Donor compliance reporting
tasks: Design source ingestion and document-extraction boundaries
Choose operational versus analytical models
Define shipment, inventory and distribution facts
Model lots, containers, programs and beneficiaries
Plan validation and exception handling
Write SQL logic for stock expiring within 60 days
Define auditability and access controls
constraints: Some offices sync only once daily
Source spreadsheets contain blank required fields
Corrections must preserve an audit trail

internal.assessment_focus: The learner should distinguish ingesting uncertain source data from accepting it into trusted analytical tables.

hints: Untrusted incoming rows need a place to land before becoming official records.
Use staging plus validation/quarantine, then model shipment lifecycle, stock snapshots and delivery events separately.
Lot and expiration date may be required in the inventory grain; preserve source documents and correction lineage.
follow_up_complications: A donor changes reporting categories mid-year.
A container contains the same product in multiple lots.
Country offices need offline operation and later synchronization.
challenges.review_exercise: Write the grain of a stock snapshot that survives both multiple lots per product and corrections to a shipment.

challenges.title: National Retail Chain Modernization

student.scenario: A retailer with 120 stores has normalized point-of-sale and inventory databases. Headquarters relies on emailed spreadsheets and wants a governed enterprise analytics platform.
requirements: Same-day sales
Daily inventory
Promotion effectiveness
Supplier performance
Store and product hierarchy history
Self-service departmental marts
tasks: Compare Kimball, Inmon and hybrid approaches
Recommend an architecture
Define enterprise conformed dimensions
Design sales, inventory and supplier facts
Plan incremental loads
Write SQL logic for promotion lift
Define semantic ownership and access
constraints: On-premises sources and cloud analytics
Six years of history
Budget favors staged delivery by domain

internal.assessment_focus: Methodology must follow organizational and delivery needs, not ideology.

hints: Consider both enterprise consistency and incremental business value.
A hybrid can combine governed integration with dimensional marts.
Promotion analysis needs an explicit comparison baseline and careful grain, not only promoted sales totals.
follow_up_complications: Finance and marketing define net revenue differently.
A store closes and later reopens under another format.
Supplier lead-time data arrives only weekly.
challenges.review_exercise: Write a three-row decision matrix comparing Kimball, Inmon and hybrid against delivery speed and enterprise consistency.

challenges.title: Insurance Claims Analytics and Fraud Signals

student.scenario: An insurer combines policy administration, claims, payments, adjuster notes, repair-shop files and external fraud scores. Claims evolve over months and can reopen after closure.
requirements: Claim-cycle performance
Paid and reserved amounts
Loss ratios
Fraud investigation queues
Point-in-time policy and customer attributes
Auditable model inputs
tasks: Design layered architecture for structured and text data
Define accumulating, transaction and snapshot facts
Model claim reopening
Choose SCD strategies
Design a fraud-feature pipeline without mixing training and future data
Write logic for claim duration and current reserve
Define governance and model lineage
constraints: Personally sensitive data
Claims can be backdated
Regulators require reproducible decisions

internal.assessment_focus: The solution must preserve lifecycle, financial movements and point-in-time correctness independently.
common_traps: Current policy values applied to old claims
Reserve treated as additive across dates

hints: A claim has milestones, money movements and changing balances.
Those needs usually imply more than one fact type.
Build fraud features using only data available at the prediction timestamp and version the exact inputs.
follow_up_complications: A catastrophe creates 100 times normal daily volume.
A closed claim reopens twice.
A new privacy rule limits adjuster-note retention.
challenges.review_exercise: State the point-in-time correctness rule for one fraud feature and one loss-ratio measure.

challenges.title: Energy Utility Smart-Meter Platform

student.scenario: An electric utility receives 15-minute smart-meter readings, outage events, billing transactions, weather data and technician work orders.
requirements: Near-real-time outage maps
Daily consumption analytics
Billing reconciliation
Demand forecasting
Meter and customer-location history
Detection of missing or impossible readings
tasks: Design streaming and batch paths
Choose raw and curated storage
Define event and snapshot grains
Handle late/corrected readings
Model meter replacement and premise history
Write daily consumption aggregation logic
Define quality SLAs and replay
constraints: Twenty million meters
Readings may arrive three days late
Billing totals must be reproducible

internal.assessment_focus: Event time and processing time must be distinguished, with correction and replay policies.

hints: When did the reading occur versus when was it received?
Use event-time processing, watermarks and replayable raw data.
Version meter-to-premise/customer relationships; reconcile curated interval usage to billing snapshots.
follow_up_complications: A daylight-saving transition creates duplicated local timestamps.
A meter firmware bug reports negative values.
Regulators require recalculating a prior tariff period.
challenges.review_exercise: Write the event-time vs processing-time policy for one reading that arrives three days late.

challenges.title: Global Logistics Control Tower

student.scenario: A logistics company tracks bookings, containers, ports, GPS devices, customs milestones, invoices and delivery confirmations across carriers.
requirements: Current shipment status
Milestone cycle times
On-time delivery
Cost by route and carrier
Historical port and carrier attributes
Exception alerts
tasks: Define canonical business keys across carriers
Design lifecycle and cost facts
Choose role-playing dates
Build ingestion for APIs, EDI and GPS
Handle missing/duplicate milestones
Write logic for on-time percentage
Define operational alerts versus analytical reporting
constraints: Carrier event formats differ
Events may arrive out of order
Shipment IDs are not globally unique

internal.assessment_focus: Carrier-specific identities and event vocabularies must be mapped into a durable canonical model.
common_traps: Assuming milestone order equals arrival order
Mixing latest status with immutable event history

hints: Source identifiers need a carrier context.
Keep immutable milestone events and derive/update a lifecycle snapshot.
Use a canonical event vocabulary, source-key mapping and explicit event timestamps for KPI calculations.
follow_up_complications: A carrier retransmits its last 30 days of events.
One container is split across two final deliveries.
Customs changes the required milestone sequence.
challenges.review_exercise: Write the canonical key rule for one shipment that appears in three carriers' systems.

challenges.title: Order Fulfillment Lifecycle

student.scenario: Orders pass through placed, paid, allocated, picked, packed, shipped, delivered and sometimes cancelled milestones. Management wants cycle time, backlog and bottleneck analysis.
requirements: One order can ship in multiple packages
Individual lines can be cancelled
Current backlog and historical milestone performance
Warehouse and carrier can change before shipment
tasks: Choose the lifecycle grain or grains
Determine whether to use accumulating snapshots, transactions or both
Define milestone date roles
Model partial shipments
Identify useful facts and dimensions
constraints: Milestones may arrive late or be corrected

internal.assessment_focus: The chosen accumulating-snapshot grain must survive partial fulfillment.
common_traps: One row per order despite split lines/packages

hints: Ask what can independently move through the lifecycle.
Order line or fulfillment package may be safer than order header grain.
Use role-playing dates for milestones and consider immutable event facts alongside a lifecycle snapshot.
follow_up_complications: Packages can be consolidated after picking.
Delivered orders may be returned.
The same line can be fulfilled by two warehouses.
challenges.review_exercise: Write one accumulating-snapshot grain statement that survives a partial shipment.

challenges.title: Marketing Campaign Attribution

student.scenario: Marketing wants campaign performance across email, paid search, social and affiliate channels. A sale may have many prior touchpoints and attribution rules change over time.
requirements: First-touch, last-touch and multi-touch views
Do not duplicate total revenue
Campaign names and channel groupings change
Analysts must reproduce previously published results
Use Tools and deliverables for each separate model or pipeline; save required evidence before completing. Explain cross-artifact decisions in your answer.
tasks: Define event and attribution grains
Model the many-to-many relationship
Choose where allocation weights live
Handle changing campaign attributes and attribution rules
Explain additive behavior of allocated revenue
constraints: Touchpoints are retained for 13 months
Orders can be refunded

internal.assessment_focus: Allocation weights must total one at a declared rule version and grain.
common_traps: Joining touchpoints directly and duplicating revenue

hints: A direct one-to-many join can multiply sale value.
Use a bridge/attribution fact with weights at sale-touchpoint-rule grain.
Version attribution runs and ensure weights sum to one per sale and rule version before allocating revenue.
follow_up_complications: Offline store visits become touchpoints.
A privacy request removes a user's web events.
Finance wants results under both original and current attribution rules.
challenges.review_exercise: Write the weight-sum rule for one sale and check it against three touchpoints.

challenges.title: Hotel Occupancy and Reservations

student.scenario: A hotel group needs booking, occupancy, cancellation and revenue analytics. Reservations span dates, can change rooms and may be cancelled before arrival.
requirements: Occupancy by night
Booking lead time
Cancellation rate
Revenue by stay date and booking date
Room type history
tasks: Define reservation and room-night grains
Choose fact types
Model booking, arrival, departure and cancellation dates
Classify room availability and occupancy measures
Explain how to avoid counting a three-night stay as one occupied night
constraints: Rates can vary by night
A reservation can include several rooms

internal.assessment_focus: Room-night grain is central to occupancy and nightly rates.

hints: The business sells nights, not merely reservations.
Consider one row per reserved room per stay date.
Use separate date roles and, if needed, a daily availability/occupancy snapshot for capacity analysis.
follow_up_complications: Guests switch rooms mid-stay.

WITH line_totals AS (SELECT order_id, date_trunc('month',order_date)::DATE AS report_month, SUM(net_amount) AS amount FROM sales_line GROUP BY 1,2), eligible AS (SELECT DISTINCT order_id,campaign FROM campaign_touch), shares AS (SELECT l.report_month,l.order_id,COALESCE(e.campaign,'unattributed') AS campaign,l.amount,
       COUNT(*) OVER(PARTITION BY l.order_id,l.report_month) AS n,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY l.order_id,l.report_month ORDER BY e.campaign NULLS LAST) AS rn
       FROM line_totals l LEFT JOIN eligible e USING(order_id)), cents AS (
       SELECT report_month,campaign, CASE WHEN rn=1 THEN CAST(ROUND(amount*100,0) AS BIGINT) - CAST(FLOOR(amount*100/n) AS BIGINT)*(n-1)
       ELSE CAST(FLOOR(amount*100/n) AS BIGINT) END AS cents FROM shares)
       SELECT report_month,campaign,CAST(SUM(cents)/100.0 AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS allocated_revenue FROM cents GROUP BY 1,2

challenges.title: Design operations and defend the coffee solution

student.scenario: Northstar Coffee is a fictional subscription roastery. Customers hold subscriptions for coffee products; orders contain product lines. Design for customers, subscriptions, products, orders and order lines using names of your choice. Report USD only, for orders placed from 2026-01-01 through 2026-03-31 (the upper SQL boundary is 2026-04-01). Order statuses are fulfilled, pending and cancelled. Only fulfilled orders contribute revenue; the reporting month is the order-placement month. Line revenue is quantity × the line's unit price: quantities are positive integers 1–5 and unit prices are positive exact decimals with two places. Exclude refunds, taxes, shipping charges and execution of historical slowly changing dimensions. Use single-column integer or UUID keys and an acyclic foreign-key graph. Generator values are independent unless supported by explicit foreign-key generators; do not assert unsupported correlations between fields, dates, prices or redundant relationships. Document assumptions and limitations.
